grammar.title: Talking about the future: if + will
grammar.explanation:
We use **if** to talk about the future. **If** means maybe it happens.

After **if**, we use the present simple. We do NOT use **will** after **if**.

In the other part, we use **will**. **Will** shows what happens next.

We also use **when** and **until** for the future. After **when** and **until**, we use the present simple too.

The **teacher** says: **If** you study, you **will** learn. The **doctor** says: **If** you rest, you **will** feel better.
examples: *If* I get a job, I *will* buy a new desk. (future plan)
*If* the doctor is busy, I *will* wait in the office. (maybe future)
*If* the teacher is kind, the children *will* learn. (a good rule)
I *will* work *when* the office opens. (at that time)
I *will* not go home *until* my job is done. (up to that time)

practice.a: Never! After **if** we use the present simple. **Will** goes in the other part.

practice.q: Is this right: **If** it **will** rain, we stay home?
practice.a: No. Say: **If** it rains, we **will** stay home.

practice.q: What does **when** mean for the future?
practice.a: It means at that time. I **will** call you **when** I get home.
